title.rendered: Goodness: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 6

excerpt.rendered: Luke pauses in Acts to give Barnabas a description he gives no one else. A good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. The three phrases go together.

content.rendered:
Luke pauses in the middle of the book of Acts to give one man a description he gives no one else. Barnabas, we are told, was “a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith.” The three phrases go together. Goodness is what the Spirit produces when He fills a life.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, September 29, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 6

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In Acts 11, Luke pauses in the middle of a rapidly-moving narrative to give one man a description he gives no one else in the entire book. He is writing about the early Jerusalem church sending a representative up to Antioch, where the gospel had begun to spread among the Gentiles. The man they sent was Barnabas. And Luke describes him in a sentence that has framed how the church has thought about goodness ever since. “For he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great many people were added to the Lord” (Acts 11:24 NKJV). Three phrases in one sentence, and Luke means them to go together. Good. Full of the Holy Spirit. Full of faith. In New Testament thinking, these three go together because they cannot be pulled apart. Goodness is what the Holy Spirit produces when He fills a life. And that fullness is what Paul is naming, six chapters back in Galatians, as the sixth fruit of the Spirit. Agathōsunē.

The Greek word agathōsunē is closely related to agathos, the word for good. But it is not merely the abstract quality of being good in a philosophical sense. It is active, engaged, generous goodness that shows up in real behaviour. It is the goodness of a person who does the right thing when nobody is watching. It is the goodness of a person who gives generously when they could have kept. It is the goodness of a person who defends the reputation of an absent friend. It is the goodness of a person who tells the truth when a lie would be easier. Barnabas was exactly that kind of person. When he first appears in Acts 4, he sells a field and lays the proceeds at the apostles’ feet. When Saul of Tarsus is converted and the Jerusalem church is too afraid to receive him, Barnabas is the one who takes Saul by the hand and vouches for him. When the church in Antioch needs a leader, Barnabas goes to Tarsus to fetch Saul and brings him in. When Mark deserts them on a missionary journey, Barnabas is the one who eventually gives Mark a second chance. Every scene we have of Barnabas shows him doing generous good.

The Passion Translation opens up the practical dimension: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action, a life full of virtue, faith that prevails, gentleness of heart, and strength of spirit” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). A life full of virtue. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love, joy (gladness), peace, patience (an even temper, forbearance), kindness, goodness (benevolence)” (Galatians 5:22 AMPC). Benevolence. Well-wishing that turns into well-doing.

Goodness is one of the most testable fruits because it shows up in behaviour that a stranger can observe. The kind of goodness the Spirit produces cannot be manufactured for a Sunday service and then forgotten by Monday morning. It is a settled orientation of the whole life. It is the difference between the appearance of goodness and the reality of it. And when the Holy Spirit is at work in a life, the people around that person begin to notice something they do not always have the vocabulary to describe. They just know that this person can be trusted. This person is safe. This person is good.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the fruit the Spirit is growing in you. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, ask the Spirit today to produce Barnabas-shaped goodness in your ordinary life. In the small decisions. In the moments when nobody is watching. In the generous gesture that costs you something. In the defence of the absent friend. In the second chance you give the one who has disappointed you. That kind of goodness is not a personality trait. It is a fruit. And the Spirit is producing it in every believer who will yield to His work and refuse to settle for the appearance of goodness when the reality is on offer.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that goodness is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. Barnabas-shaped goodness. Active. Engaged. Generous. Real. Today I ask You to produce that goodness in me. In the small decisions. In the moments when nobody is watching. In the generous gesture that costs me something. I refuse to settle for the appearance of goodness when Your Spirit is producing the reality. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Goodness is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. Active, engaged, generous, real. I am a good person, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. The people around me can trust me.
